title: Animal Origin
subtitle: What the label says. And what it doesn't.
intro: Some ingredients come from animals. Some might. And some hide behind technical names that give nothing away. BOTIA reads the label and flags what it finds — so you can decide.
why_body: Whether you avoid animal products for ethical, religious, dietary or personal reasons — the label is not always on your side. An ingredient can be animal-derived and still appear as a code, a chemical name, or simply 'natural flavouring'. BOTIA makes that visible.
how_confirmed: Some ingredients are always from animals: gelatine, carmine (E120), shellac (E904), beeswax, lactose, casein, whey, honey. When BOTIA finds these, there is no ambiguity.
how_ambiguous: Other ingredients may come from animals or plants depending on the manufacturer: E471, E472, lecithins (E322), glycerol (E422), enzymes, natural flavourings. The label does not say which. Only the manufacturer knows.
vegan_body: There is no single EU regulation defining 'vegan' as a specific certified standard. However, any vegan claim is subject to general food labelling law — EU Regulation 1169/2011 prohibits misleading information. If a product is labelled vegan but contains animal-derived ingredients, the manufacturer faces legal liability. BOTIA reads the ingredient list, not the marketing claim.
can_2: Flag ingredients that may be animal-derived when the label does not specify.
can_3: Make visible what the label leaves unclear.
cannot_1: Certify that a product is vegan or vegetarian.
cannot_2: Confirm the exact origin of ambiguous ingredients — only the manufacturer can.
cannot_3: Detect animal-derived processing aids not listed on the label.
closing: BOTIA reads what is declared. For full certainty, contact the manufacturer or look for a certified vegan logo.
